studies.title: How much reasoning is enough?
studies.summary: Luna medium, low, and none. Reader and writer results kept separate.
studies.sample: 13 reader + 4 writer inputs · 53 calls including calibration
studies.finding: Keep one medium default for now. Lower effort saved small amounts on reader answers; four writer inputs do not establish a routing policy.
conditions: Controlled synthetic text fixtures with real provider calls. Saved outputs are historical observations, not simulated scores.
GPT-6 Luna, OpenAI provider, no fallback. Effort is the only explicit model parameter changed; temperature is omitted.
Full 128,000 output allowance for every call; every response ended normally. Thirteen identical reader inputs and four extraction inputs per profile, plus two separate calibrations.
Three blocks rotate profile order. Actual cache-read and cache-write tokens remain in the original metrics. Reader contexts use the retained Qwen3-Embedding-8B 4096-dimensional retrieval.
Fifty-three calls; new settled spend $0.016351425. Reader and writer costs in the tables exclude the two calibrations.
limitations: A small diagnostic pass, not a general intelligence ranking or a statistically stable quality order. Repeated questions share facts and are not independent projects.
A matching literal quote proves source binding. It does not prove semantic entailment, complete answers, tenant isolation, or customer acceptance.
Missing or infrastructure-invalid measurements remain unavailable. They are not semantic zeros. Research evidence is neither Calibration nor Official Core evidence.
No native storage, reconciliation, retrieval, or final Agent tool loop was rerun.
None saved about $0.04 per thousand reader answers in this workload. Four writer samples do not justify a routing policy. No default configuration changed.
The original report suggested exploring none for routine extraction. The later interpretation shown here retains one medium default. The original report remains byte-identical.
